summary: Circa-1935 lookout cabin on a 20 ft timber tower in Sequoia-Kings Canyon; newspaper clippings describe staff and a 1945 lightning fire; register says nothing remains.

facts.design: US Forest Service California Region 5 Plan BC-301 cabin atop a 20 foot enclosed timber tower
facts.status_note: Nothing remains at the site, according to the register; removal date unknown.
facts.agency: National Park Service, Sequoia-Kings Canyon National Park

events.note: Built circa 1935 to USFS California Region 5 plan BC-301: cabin on a 20 ft enclosed timber tower (register)
A.S. Walker named as lookout at the Cahoon Rock Station (July 1936 clipping)
Lightning struck 150 yards from the station; Rose Vaughn fought the fire with a shovel and reported three more fires (July 1945 clipping)
Rose Vaughn left for the remote Cahoon lookout (June 1946 clipping)
Vaughn had held the job nine years per an August 1951 clipping; she fell ill and was taken off by pack train

corrections.why: The register describes a 20 foot enclosed timber tower, about 6.1 m. The record's 152.4 m (500 ft) is not supported by any source read. The 6.1 m figure is the tower height; the cab sits on top of it.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record uses the register's 2,831 m (9,288 ft). The clippings give 9,000 ft (1936), 10,500 ft (1945) and 9,200 ft (1951). These are not reconciled; the story reports the difference and does not choose one.

notes_for_editor: Record height_m 152.4 is wrong; the register describes a 20 ft tower. Elevation differs across sources (9,000 / 9,200 / 10,500 ft in clippings vs 9,288 ft in the register). The 'today' statement rests on one register sentence; no independent site description or access information was found. Newspaper text comes from a secondary transcription page; originals were not checked. One 1951 clipping spells the name Vaughan. NPS and NIFC social posts on Rose Vaughn appeared in search results but were not read. Calisphere image pages render only with JavaScript, so no photos were added.
